Defects internal to a single unit are judged in that unit's own review; this review covers contradictions, duplicate scope, missing dependencies and shared interfaces between units.

Units whose depends_on is satisfied may be implemented in parallel: add-fake-oidc, add-audit-chain, add-identity-model and add-pdp-cedar together, then add-api-conventions and add-web-ui-kit together. I found no shared file edited by two units that may run at the same time.

findings.text: Dependencies are added in two different ways, and the units disagree. add-web-ui-kit task 9.1 has the implementer add axe-core 4.14.0 to the root package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml. Its a11y-setup check also needs node_modules/axe-core/axe.min.js to be installed. The other units say otherwise: add-pdp-cedar gets @cedar-policy/cedar-wasm from the scaffold, not from the unit; add-api-conventions design decision 8 calls package.json an owner file; add-fake-oidc says the L4 gates have no network. If package.json is owner-only, or the run is offline, task 9.1 cannot be done. The plan should either have the scaffold install axe-core, as it does for cedar-wasm, or say explicitly that a unit may change package.json and the lockfile and install a package.

add-web-data-kit puts DataTable.tsx, Field.tsx, Form.tsx and SchemaForm.tsx in web/src/kit/data/. Its stated reason is that add-web-ui-kit's frozen scenario "Documentation matches the component files" expects exactly five .tsx files in web/src/kit. It adds: if that scenario looks into subdirectories, 'the orchestrator must change it'. But add-web-ui-kit task 8.1 only says 'listing the .tsx files of web/src/kit with node:fs'. It never says the listing is non-recursive. If the earlier unit lists recursively, the later unit turns it red. add-web-ui-kit should state that only direct children of web/src/kit count.

add-api-pep's requirement "Every route of every listener comes from defineRoute" (scenario 'The real engine') says the public server's defined routes are exactly six. add-api-conventions task 5.2 adds GET /api/v1/openapi.json and edits api-pep's frozen test src/main.api.test.ts::The real engine. It does not amend api-pep's spec text, so the merged specs contradict each other. The batch also has no single rule on another unit's frozen tests. add-api-conventions edits one, and add-web-ui-kit edits web-shell's e2e/test_m0_skeleton.py. Yet add-web-ui-kit refuses to touch add-supply-chain-gate's frozen policy scenario, and add-web-data-kit works around add-web-ui-kit's frozen keyboard scenario. The plan should state one rule and amend the api-pep requirement.

The default-tenant seeding may conflict with tenant B, and no unit settles it. add-web-sign-in relies on 'ensureDefaultTenant refuses a second tenant', which is why it inserts tenant B by hand. add-oidc-login decision 12 has oidcPart.seed call ensureDefaultTenant(pool, E2E_TENANT_NAME) 'after every reset'. add-web-sign-in says 'a reset re-runs every seed', and its scenario 'Tenant B is created and its organisation provisioned' runs oidcPart.seed and tenantBPart.seed twice on one database. No unit says whether ensureDefaultTenant still returns the existing default once tenant B exists, or whether /reset removes tenant B before oidcPart.seed runs again. If it refuses, the second seed fails, along with every fresh_state reset after the first. That would break e2e/test_m1_sign_in.py and the earlier journeys.

Adding the oidc part may stop the engine from starting in every e2e journey. Once parts/25-oidc.ts exists, the stack env contains URSITOARE_OIDC_ISSUER. add-oidc-login's 'Missing prerequisites' scenario then requires URSITOARE_ENGINE_KEY_FILE and URSITOARE_DATABASE_URL. Decision 12 gives oidcPart only URSITOARE_OIDC_ISSUER and URSITOARE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE, and the part's own test supplies the engine key file separately. No unit says the e2e stack provides the engine key. If it does not, the M0, web-kit and sign-in journeys all fail at engine start, and no unit's tasks would catch it.

Web messages for later error codes are handed off to a unit that does not take them. add-web-ui-kit decision 4 says add-api-conventions 'adds the rest' of the messages (BAD_REQUEST, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE and others). add-api-conventions touches no web file and registers no message. add-web-data-kit and add-web-sign-in both rule it out of their own scope. So CURSOR_INVALID, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS, BAD_REQUEST, PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE, UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE and WEB_NOT_BUILT keep FALLBACK_MESSAGE, against add-web-ui-kit's requirement that 'every API error code' has one text.

Three units each write their own sorted-key JSON serialisation with different rules: add-audit-chain's canonicalize (RFC 8785, refuses undefined, allows safe bigint), add-pdp-cedar's canonicalJson and requestDigest (omits undefined properties, refuses bigint), and add-api-conventions' requestDigestOf (undefined as null). add-pdp-cedar acknowledges the overlap. Separately, two units declare the same KeyMaterial { reveal(): string } interface: src/audit and src/api/cursor.ts.

The code count does not match. add-web-sign-in relies on 'a sign-in refusal is a 302 to /sign-in?error=<one of ten codes>' and lists 'the ten /sign-in?error= codes' as taken from add-oidc-login. add-oidc-login defines nine sign-in codes (OIDC_LOGIN_EXPIRED through OIDC_INTERNAL). SESSION_ENDED is add-web-sign-in's own code, not the server's.

add-fake-oidc decision 10(a) refuses a token request unless the content type is application/x-www-form-urlencoded. It does not say whether media-type parameters are accepted. add-oidc-login's exchangeCode posts 'form-encoded' and does not fix the header. fetch with a URLSearchParams body sends 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8', so an exact string match in the fake would turn every real exchange into a 400.

findings.text: Task 4.1 reads the clock twice. It says to call `formatAt(opts.clock.now())` first and use that for the hash, then to insert `at` "from `clock.now().toISOString()`". Decision 2 and the requirement say `at` is a single injected instant. With `systemClock`, the two calls can land in different milliseconds. The stored `at` then differs from the hashed `at`, and `verifyChain` reports `hash` for an untampered production row, which corrupts the chain silently. Every append and verify scenario uses `fixedClock`, so no test can catch this before an unreviewed merge. Fix: say the clock is read once and the same Date is used for both `formatAt` and the stored `at`. Add a scenario with a clock that returns a different instant on each `now()` call and expects `verifyChain` to report ok.

The scenario "An event must match the head" expects "a 31-byte hash ... reject with { code: "23514" }". This cannot pass. `audit_event_head_match` is a BEFORE INSERT row trigger, and those run before CHECK constraints. `audit_head.hash` has the constraint `CHECK (octet_length(hash) = 32)`, so a 31-byte `NEW.hash` can never equal the head's hash. The trigger therefore always raises U0802, never 23514. The scenario should either say `prev_hash` or expect U0802. The scenario also leaves out the head state that lets `origin "x"`, an `mk_jti` with origin `ursitoare`, and `seq 0` get past the trigger to reach the CHECK. Each needs a head with the same seq and hash first, and seq 0 needs the head at seq 0 with a hash equal to `NEW.hash`.

The scenario "Nobody can change or remove" inserts "one event" and then expects the owner's UPDATE and DELETE on both `audit_event_default` and "a partition made by `ensurePartitions`" to reject with U0801. One row can live in only one leaf. On the other leaf the statement matches zero rows, so the row-level trigger never fires and the statement succeeds. The scenario cannot pass as written. It should seed one row in each leaf (each needs its own head advance because of the head-match trigger), give the `at` values, and say that `ensurePartitions` runs before the inserts.

Nothing in the material lets anyone check the known-answer constants, and one of them looks wrong. H1 (`e5caec3c...`) and H2 (`e5ca9b27...`) start with the same 16 bits, which happens for independent SHA-256 digests with probability 1/65536. The test plan says these are fixed strings computed outside the code under test, so the implementer cannot recompute them. If H1, H2 or the `anchorMac` answer `75e40e23...` is wrong, the scenarios "Known answers", "First and second event" and "Known answer and idempotence" are stuck with no legitimate fix. Attach the reproduction: the exact input bytes and the script with its output for H1, H2 and the anchor MAC.

The owner can erase or shorten a chain without the engine key, and nothing reports it. No TRUNCATE trigger exists, and row triggers do not fire on TRUNCATE. `audit_head` has no protection at all, and the owner can delete anchors after disabling `audit_anchor_append_only`. The owner alone can cut the tail (or truncate everything), lower or delete the head and remove later anchors, and `verifyChain` still returns `{ ok: true, ... }`. This contradicts three statements: the proposal's "nobody, not even the database owner, can change without being noticed", Security §2's "a trigger stops every role", and Security §5's residual risk, which names only "the owner role plus the engine key". The author has to choose: protect against TRUNCATE (and the head or anchor deletion), with an owner TRUNCATE scenario, or restate the outcome and the residual risk so they match what is built.

The requirement "The audit tables are append-only..." ("reject UPDATE and DELETE ... for every role with SQLSTATE U0801") and the proposal ("an update or delete by any role fails with SQLSTATE U0801") contradict their own scenario, which expects `42501` for the app role. The scenario is the correct one: the privilege check runs before the trigger. The requirement and proposal text should say the same.

`wrapStoreError` wraps any `code` made of exactly five characters from `0-9A-Z`. Node errno codes such as `EPIPE`, `EPERM`, `EBADF` and `EINTR` match that rule, so a lost connection could come back as `AUDIT_STORE_FAILED` with `sqlstate: "EPIPE"`. The failure table says "Postgres down, connection lost: the driver error propagates unchanged".

Tasks 4.1 and 6.1 send errors through `wrapStoreError`, but tasks 5.1, 5.2 and 6.2 never say whether `verifyChain` does. Decision 9 and the failure table are general, so how `verifyChain` reports a SQL error to later callers (audit API, CLI) is not fixed.

`validateEvent` calls `canonicalize(payload)` with the payload at depth 0. `canonicalEvent` places the payload one level down inside the event document. A payload with exactly 64 nested containers therefore passes validation and then fails `too_deep` in `chainHash`, after appendAudit has already run the head SELECT FOR UPDATE and possibly the INSERT. That contradicts "no SQL ran" for invalid payloads. Either the depth limits should match or the scenario should state this behaviour.

The spec does not say what `anchorHead` does when the event at the head's seq is missing or duplicated; task 6.1 only says "read the event hash at seq and compare". It also does not say what `verifyChain` does with `fromSeq` when two rows share seq `fromSeq - 1`; the `SELECT hash ... WHERE seq = $2` lookup returns two rows.

Decision 10 is a rule and nothing enforces it. A caller that has appended and then calls `appendAuditCommitted` for the same tenant hangs indefinitely on its own head lock, with no lock_timeout and no detection. The same happens when the caller already holds the pool's last connection. The failure behaviour, at least that it hangs, should be stated for later units.

In the failure table, the row "Invalid event, secret key, oversized or non-JSON payload" maps "oversized" to `AUDIT_CANONICAL_INVALID`. The requirement and task 2.1 make an oversized payload `AUDIT_EVENT_INVALID` with reason `payload_too_large`.

findings.text: No task is allowed to implement the token endpoint's body limit and its socket handling. Design decision 2 puts body reading in server.ts, fixes Reply = { status, headers, body } and says "a handler never touches the socket". Decision 10(a) requires that a body over 65536 bytes gets 413 invalid_request with the "socket destroyed after the answer". Task 2.1's scope covers "design.md decisions 2 to 4, 12 and 13" and leaves out decision 10, so the body reader it builds is never told about a limit. Task 2.3 says it "adds only that route" to server.ts. So the handler cannot destroy the socket, 2.1 is not asked to enforce the limit, and 2.3 may not change the body reader. The "Bad requests" scenario (65537 bytes → 413) is tested only in token.test.ts (2.3), so 2.1's gate will not catch the omission. 2.3 will then either stall or quietly break its own scope rule. The spec also does not say whether the 65536 limit applies to the authorize POST or to every body. Fix: add decision 10(a)'s limit and destroy to 2.1's scope and say which routes it covers, or give Reply a close-connection flag that the server acts on.

The login-page scenario "Labels and structure" quotes literal markup: `<input id="username" name="username">`, `<input id="password" name="password" type="password">` and `<button type="submit">Sign In</button>` "exists". Design decision 8 adds `autocomplete` attributes and `<button id="kc-login" type="submit">`, so those literal strings would not appear in the page. Task 1.5 says the page is checked with "string checks", which makes a literal `includes` test likely. Once that test is frozen at red, green would have to drop `id="kc-login"`/`autocomplete` or fail. State that the checks are by attribute (for/id pairing, attribute presence), not by exact markup.

Decision 7 says the ID token carries `auth_time` but never gives its value, and no scenario asserts it. The code record in decision 9 (`{ code, clientId, redirectUri, challenge, scope, nonce, username, sid, expiresAt }`) stores no authentication time, and `mintJwt`'s options (`MintOptions & { sid?: string }`) have no field for one. So an exchanged ID token can only carry the exchange time, not the sign-in time. Consumers that check `auth_time` (for example with max_age) depend on this value.

The requirement says mintToken returns a token "wrong in exactly one way" for "the given user, client and kind". The claim-flaw scenarios fix only an alice ID token with `nonce: "n-2"`. Several other inputs are left open. With `kind: "access"` (no nonce claim under decision 7), or with no `nonce`, `missing_nonce` gives a valid token. With no nonce, `wrong_nonce` has no defined value and no defined error. For users other than alice, or a scope without `organization`, the value of `two_organizations` is not given. The spec should say whether these inputs throw FAKE_OIDC_BAD_OPTIONS or what claims they produce.

For the `hs256_public_key` flaw, the spec does not say whether the header carries a `kid`. JwtSigner's HS256 variant has `kid?`. An algorithm-confusion token is usually built with the RSA key's kid, so a verifier would pick the RSA key, and consumers' negative tests depend on which header they get.

The proposal lists `index.ts` under "Files implemented (stubs from the scaffold)" and design.md lists what it re-exports. No task owns it, yet task 3.1's test "imports only from ./index.ts". If the scaffold stub does not already contain the re-exports, no task is told to write them.

Some behaviour fixed in the design has no scenario: `registerRedirect` throwing `FAKE_OIDC_BAD_REDIRECT` (non-http(s), userinfo, fragment) and `FAKE_OIDC_UNKNOWN_CLIENT` for an unknown `opts.clientId` (decision 12), and the code store's limit of 1000 entries with the oldest dropped (Data model). Only the start-time path (`redirectUri: "javascript:x"` → FAKE_OIDC_START_FAILED) is covered.

Decision 10(a) requires content type `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and answers 400 otherwise, but does not say whether media-type parameters are allowed. `fetch` with a `URLSearchParams` body sends `application/x-www-form-urlencoded;charset=UTF-8`, and that is the usual path for RP libraries used by add-oidc-login. An exact string comparison would refuse real clients unless the fake's own tests happen to use exactly that path.

Decision 14 fixes the assertions for discovery, JWKS, tokens, the two refusal checks and the logout target. It does not fix the scope the contract requests (the `organization` assertion needs `organization` in it), what `userinfo with the access token`, `wrong password shows the error`, `code is single use` and `logout ends the session` assert, which redirect URI the `redirect uri must match exactly` check sends, or whether each check gets its own cookie jar. A shared jar would let Keycloak's SSO cookie skip the form when add-stack-conformance runs the contract later. The rule "asserts only what Keycloak also does" cannot be checked without Keycloak.

Login details are left open. The label reads `Username or email`, but decision 9 looks users up by lower-cased username only, so whether an email address signs in is not stated. Whether the re-rendered username field shows the name as typed or lower-cased is also not stated.

The logout refusal ("400 `invalid_request`") does not say whether the body is JSON `{"error":"invalid_request"}` or HTML, even though it is a browser-facing endpoint. Separately, the userinfo requirement says "access token", but decision 11 never checks `typ: "Bearer"`, so an ID token would be accepted as a bearer token.

findings.text: design.md § Behaviour details (upsertUserFromClaims) says optional claims are trimmed and then 'names are cut to 200 characters'. The display-name fallback chain (name → preferredUsername → email → subject) is also 'cut to 200'. Nothing says to trim again after the cut. The migration CHECK on ursitoare."user" is `display_name = btrim(display_name) AND char_length(display_name) BETWEEN 1 AND 200`. Take a claim that the spec accepts as valid (requireText and the optional-claim rule both allow internal spaces) of 201 or more characters with a space at index 199. Cutting it leaves a trailing space, the INSERT or UPDATE fails with SQLSTATE 23514, and sign-in throws a raw driver error. That breaks the SHALL of 'The first sign-in creates a human user and its IdP link' and the update path of 'Later sign-ins…'. No scenario covers it: sub-5 is 300 'x' with no spaces. The same sentence also says 'characters' where the rest of the design says 'code units', and char_length counts code points. A code-unit slice can split a surrogate pair. node-pg would then store U+FFFD while the returned User keeps the lone surrogate, so every later 'Unchanged' comparison sees a difference and writes. The author should state: the unit of the cut, re-trim after the cut, and what happens if the result is empty. A scenario with a space at the cut point should be added.

Three scenarios treat cross-tenant userId difference as if the system guaranteed it, but the primary key is (tenant_id, user_id), so the same id in two tenants is legal. The scenarios are: 'Same subject in two tenants…' ('the two userId values differ'), 'Get' (mallory's id gives null in a) and 'Invalid owners' (mallory's id gives IDENTITY_OWNER_INVALID). tasks.md 6.1 only says users are created 'with sequentialIds()' and does not say the source is shared. If each call gets a fresh sequentialIds(), alice and mallory both get usr_00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000000. Then getUser(a, mallory.userId) returns alice and createServiceAccount accepts mallory's id. The scenarios should name one shared id source, or distinct seeds per tenant.

The design.md Failure cases table says 'Bad claims, ids, names, limit, after → IDENTITY_INVALID before any SQL'. But § Behaviour details orders getUser as 'tenant check; userId must match the id pattern' and listUsers as 'tenant check; limit … after …'. The tenant check is a SQL statement (SELECT current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)). When ctx is wrong and the input is also bad, the two texts give different errors (IDENTITY_TENANT_MISMATCH vs IDENTITY_INVALID), and no scenario settles it. upsertUserFromClaims and createServiceAccount validate first, so getUser and listUsers are the inconsistent ones.

findings.text: Scenario "No values in logs, a failing audit" says that when "for a disabled user the second `connect` of the pool fails", the callback "still answers the same 302 and logs the failure". Following design.md decision 6, connect #1 is `resolveTenantForToken` (it reaches `resolveTenantBy` through `TenantPool`, which has only `connect`; add-identity-model's "connect is never called" scenario covers only claim errors, so a lookup does connect). Connect #2 is the `withTenantTx` that runs `upsertUserFromClaims`, and connect #3 is `appendAuditCommitted`. If #2 fails, the result is `OIDC_INTERNAL` and no audit is attempted, not `OIDC_USER_DISABLED`. This project freezes `*.test.ts` after red (`docs/decisions/0002`, cited in add-fake-oidc's design), so a red test written as worded cannot pass green. The intent is recoverable from the heading ("a failing audit"): it should be the connect that `appendAuditCommitted` uses, which is the third.

The requirement says that when a validated token named the tenant, the callback SHALL append `auth.login_refused` to that tenant's chain. The proposal says the same. Task 6.3 limits auditing to `OIDC_USER_DISABLED` only, and the design note "Today that is OIDC_USER_DISABLED" claims these are the same set. They are not. At least two other failures happen after a validated token resolved the tenant: `IDENTITY_INVALID` from `upsertUserFromClaims` (mapped to `OIDC_TOKEN_INVALID`), and a database error inside the tenant transaction or `createSession` (`OIDC_INTERNAL`). The SHALL requires auditing these; the task forbids it. No scenario decides between the two.

`parts/25-oidc.ts` adds `URSITOARE_OIDC_ISSUER` and `URSITOARE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE` to the e2e stack env. By this unit's own "Missing prerequisites" scenario, an issuer without `URSITOARE_ENGINE_KEY_FILE` or a database URL makes `loadConfig` throw, and the engine then fails to start. The redirect the part registers (`engineOrigin + "/auth/oidc/callback"`) also matches the engine's redirect URI only if the stack engine's `publicBaseUrl` equals `engineOrigin`. Nothing in the material shows that the stack supplies an engine key file or sets `publicBaseUrl` to `engineOrigin`. No scenario starts the stack's engine with the part present: "Start, seed and close" runs `loadConfig` with an engine key file it adds itself. Under acceptance profile `all`, this could stop the stack engine and fail every existing e2e run. The spec should state how the stack engine meets these prerequisites, or add a scenario that proves it.

Task 6.3 says `refusals.test.ts` uses "the same setup as `callback.test.ts`", and that setup provisions both `org-a` and `org-b`. The fake seeds only those two organizations, and `mintToken` has no organization option. So "an organization with no tenant" cannot be produced under that setup. The audit scenario also expects "tenant B's chain is empty" after the unknown-organization refusal, which only makes sense if `org-b` is unprovisioned in that test. The setup sentence and the scenario disagree; the spec should say how the unknown organization is made, for example a database without `org-b` provisioned.

Design decision 8 says `resolveSession` gives null when the user is not `active`. The parenthetical "a live one is then revoked and unrouted" sits next to the expiry and idle conditions, so it is unclear whether it also covers a disabled user. "Decisions made while writing" adds "A disabled user loses live sessions too". Revoking on disable would contradict the scenario "the re-enabled one resolves again". The scenario decides it, but the two statements should be reconciled (no revocation for a disabled user).

Two failure paths at logout are not settled. (1) Scenario "Provider down at logout" expects `redirect` to be `${publicBaseUrl}/sign-in`, and decision 10 says "without discovery or hint". Discovery is cached for 3600 s, so after a sign-in, logout with the provider down would still find a cached `logoutUrl`. The spec should say whether this case means a failed `discovery()` call and how the test makes it (for example a fresh `registerOidcRoutes`, or a failing `deps.fetch`). (2) The design says a database error in `resolveSession` propagates and is never null, but no scenario covers it, and the logout response when the database fails is not stated.

`OIDC_SEAL_INVALID` (engine key text under 32 characters) is listed among the error codes, but the spec does not say where it is raised (in `registerOidcRoutes`/`main` at startup, or per request) or what the caller sees. It is not one of the `/sign-in?error=` codes, and no scenario covers it. Other boundary cases are also untested and unstated: a `state` longer than 128 characters (`OIDC_BAD_REQUEST` or `OIDC_STATE_MISMATCH`?), and which code `IDENTITY_TENANT_MISMATCH` maps to ("a tenant IdentityError" is ambiguous).

Security §4 says no log holds a code, token, claim or cookie. The callback receives `code` and `state` in its query string. The scenario "No values in logs" does not say which log lines or which logger level the capturing logger checks. So the test can pass without deciding whether the server's own request log records the callback URL, and `src/api` is not among this unit's changed files. The spec should state whether the assertion covers all lines at info level or only the refusal line.

"Missing prerequisites" expects `CONFIG_SECRET_EMPTY` for a missing secret file as well as for an empty one. That depends on how the delivered `readSecretValue` treats an absent file, and the material does not show it; only its signature appears in delivered-shapes.md. The variable that the two `CONFIG_SECRET_EMPTY` errors name is also left implicit, and so is the variable for a direct `URSITOARE_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`.

Design.md states "`identity` cannot import `src/api`". Yet tasks 6.1 to 6.4 put tests under `src/identity/oidc/` that import `buildServer` from `src/api`. The material does not say whether the architecture-fitness gate exempts `*.test.ts` files.

Design decision 12 has the e2e part build "a one-connection owner pool from `databaseApi(ctx.handles).ownerUrl`". No pool constructor is listed under Interfaces taken: `createPool` from add-db-foundation is not taken, and direct `pg.Pool` use is not stated. Separately, `SessionContext.endSessionHint` is implicitly the sealed value. That follows from `resolveSession` having no engine key, and task 6.4 opens it in logout, but it is never stated, and later units (`add-api-pep`) consume this type. The design's restatement of `FakeOidc` also omits `requests()`, which the client scenarios rely on.

Design decision 8 says a session gives null when "past `expires_at`", but the scenario expects null at exactly 43200 s, which is `now >= expires_at`. Design decision 9 says the CSRF token is the SHA-256 of "32 fresh random bytes (base64url)" without saying whether the raw bytes or the base64url text are hashed. The scenario "stored `csrf_token_hash` equals the SHA-256 of the second" depends on that choice.

findings.text: PdpError shapes outside the policy stages are not fixed. For a PDP_SCHEMA_INVALID parse failure (scenario 'A bad schema is refused', schema `entity ;`), design Decision 2 fixes only `details.reason` `namespace` for the namespace case. Nothing says whether a parse failure carries `stage`, `reason` (e.g. `parse`) or neither. The message format `<code>: <stage> <ids joined by ", ">` (Decision 2) is defined only for policy-stage errors, not for options, schema or record errors. Decision 2 caps the message at 20 ids, but nothing says whether `details.ids` has the same cap.

Design Decision 9 says only that the PDP_RECORD_INVALID `details.reason` 'names the field', with one example (`decided_at`). It does not fix the full set of validated fields or their reason strings (`decision`/`policy_set_version`/`tenant_id` or camelCase `policySetVersion`/`tenantId`?). Failure cases say 'an invalid decision, id or tenant' without saying which id: `decisionId`, `runId` and `nodeId` all have 1..128 column checks. An empty `runId` could fail as PDP_RECORD_INVALID or as PDP_RECORD_FAILED with 23514. The scenario 'Invalid decisions and a failing insert' asserts only the code.

`egress: null` and a non-object `egress` are unclassified. Design Decision 8 says only 'egress omitted when absent', and Decision 7 gives the field regexes. It is not stated whether `null` counts as absent (allow, no permit) or as an invalid egress (deny, PDP_REQUEST_INVALID). Either way no permit is issued, but a test cannot decide which is correct.

In createPdp, option faults outside Decision 3's list are unspecified: a `policies` element that is not an object (e.g. `null`), or a missing `clock`/`ids`/`logger`. The result could be a PdpError PDP_OPTIONS_INVALID (with which reason?) or a raw TypeError.

`requestDigest` (Decision 8) falls back only on `TypeError`. The scenario 'A request that is not a request' sends a context whose getter throws, and `check` denies it. When that deny reaches `recordDecision`, `canonicalJson` runs the getter, and a non-TypeError throw makes `recordDecision` reject with an unclassified error, neither PDP_RECORD_INVALID nor PDP_RECORD_FAILED. That conflicts with Decision 9's aim that 'a hostile id cannot block the log of its denial'.

`toDecimal` (Decision 10): the rule 'RangeError unless n.toFixed(4) equals n' accepts `Infinity` (`toFixed` gives "Infinity") and very large values (1e21 gives "1e+21"). It then emits an `arg` that is not a valid Cedar decimal, and it does not enforce the Cedar decimal range. The request still fails closed through Cedar (PDP_REQUEST_INVALID), but the helper's contract is incomplete.

Design Decision 5 says 'Any other exception is PDP_INTERNAL, logged as { err }'. Security item 4 says 'errors and logs hold codes, ids and counts, never policy text, Cedar messages, context or entities'. A serialised `err` from the wasm, or a TypeError raised on request data, can carry exactly those. The log level and `msg` of the PDP_INTERNAL line are also unspecified, and so is whether it is logged as well as, or instead of, 'pdp deny on error'.

Some stated behaviour has no scenario: the 'pdp loaded' log line, which the proposal lists as a given interface and design Decision 6 specifies (`logger.info({ policySetVersion, policies: <count> })`, where 'count' of policies or of sources is not said); the PDP_INTERNAL path; and option reason `schema` (Decision 3). Security item 4, 'A stored permit path must never hold a credential', has no mechanism or test. It should be stated as a caller obligation or turned into an enforced, tested rule.

`canonicalJson`/`sha256Hex` in `src/pdp/digest.ts` overlap the `canonicalize` that 'Decisions made while writing' item 2 says `add-audit-chain` will own. The overlap is acknowledged ('moving later is a refactor'), but it leaves two canonical-JSON implementations in the plan with no rule that they must agree.

findings.text: Two scenarios assume `Pdp.policies` is sorted by id, but neither unit fixes that order. "Layers" expects the filtered entries `[m-a, platform-cross-tenant-forbid, t-1]`, while composition order (decision 7) is platform, then fragments, then tenant. "The platform source" expects the engine's platform entries to equal `PLATFORM_POLICY_IDS` (sorted), while decision 4 lists the policies as cross-tenant, untrusted-egress, agent-consequential, read-self. Both pass only if `Pdp.policies` is sorted by id. The add-pdp-cedar spec has one scenario whose output happens to be sorted ('The test set loads') but no requirement that says so. State the order, or have the tests compare sorted lists.

`sampleRequest` (design decision 9) is a given interface, but its values are only partly stated. The 'fixed context' names empty taint, `run_initiator`, `provider` and `region`. It leaves out required context attributes of `activate_flow` (`flow_capabilities`, `review_profile`), `invoke_llm` (`args`) and `invoke_tool` (`args`, `sod_excluded`, `approvals`, `approvers_by_role`, `node_fingerprint`). It also leaves out the required attributes of Flow, Task and Block resources (`owner_team`, `reviewed`, `run`, `kind`, `flow`). Strict request validation rejects undeclared context attributes, so one context cannot serve all 25 actions; it has to be per action, and the design does not say so. Also, 'principal `User::"tenant_a/alice"` of tenant `principalTenant`' does not say whether the uid changes when `principalTenant` is `tenant_b`. The rule that the cross-tenant table first checks the same-tenant request is `allow` catches a schema-invalid sample, so this is minor.

`loadPolicyFragments` (decision 6) states outcomes only for a bad `srcDir` and for bad `*.cedar` entries. It is silent on an unreadable `<module>/policy` directory, a file removed between `readdir` and `readFile`, and a `<module>` or `policy` entry that is a symlink to a directory. Under 'other files and directories are ignored', a symlink is not `isDirectory()` and would be skipped silently. That conflicts with the stated rule that 'a forbid must never be skipped silently'. Also unstated: whether `fragment_name` reports every bad entry or only the first.

`createPolicyEngine` checks `srcDir`, `tenantPolicies` and `toolArgs`. Its behaviour is not stated for `opts` being null or undefined, for missing or invalid `clock`, `ids` or `logger`, or for `buildSchema(null)` (only `toolArgs: null` is covered).

The scenario "Policies and roles" does not give the `actions` argument; the expected order of the results implies `ACTION_NAMES`. It also gives no source ids or `@id`s for the two tenant policies. The 'kind service' principal is assumed to be alice with no roles.

The scenario titled "A fragment or tenant source cannot reuse an id" has only fragment cases, with no tenant-source case. A tenant source reusing a platform id is covered only indirectly, by add-pdp-cedar's scenario on `createPdp`.

findings.text: SchemaForm passes values to Field and Form that their own models reject, so an untrusted schema can crash the render. Task 4.2 says SchemaForm renders "one `Field` per field" (idPrefix from useId()) inside a `Form`. But `fieldModel` (task 3.2) throws KIT_PROP_INVALID when the name fails `isFieldName`, the label is not 1 to 80 characters, or the error is over 500. `formModel` (task 3.3) throws on a duplicate or invalid name and on more than 100 fields. Task 4.1 can produce each of these. (a) An `unsupported` field whose name fails `isFieldName`: the `__proto__` property in "Names and required", a key such as `a-b`, or `""`. Its name and label are "the name cleaned of control characters, cut to 64", and for `""` the label is blank. (b) A valid name whose derived label is longer than 80: a 64-character alternating-case name like `aBcD…` gets a space before every capital, about 96 characters. (c) An `error` of "Unsupported: " + reason, where `type "<type>" is not supported` and `keyword "<key>" is not supported` embed schema text of any length, so it can pass 500. (d) `required` entries with no property, which add `unsupported` fields with no cap and no de-duplication, so `required: ["ghost","ghost"]` or more than 100 such names breaks `formModel`. Security §3 and §5 call the schema untrusted and list a `__proto__` property as a handled abuse case, but the specified rendering throws on it. No test exercises SchemaForm, so nothing would catch this before merge. The author must say how unsupported or invalid-named fields render (for example without `Field`, with index-based ids), which names reach `Form.fields`, and how labels, reasons and ghost `required` entries are bounded.

DataTable's loading label can exceed what add-web-ui-kit's LoadingState accepts. Task 2.2 allows a caption of 1 to 120 characters and sets `loadingLabel` to `Loading ` + caption, so up to 128 characters, and DataTable renders `LoadingState` with it while the first page loads. add-web-ui-kit's scenario "Invalid properties" makes `loadingStateModel` throw KIT_PROP_INVALID for an 81-character label. Any caption of 73 characters or more therefore makes DataTable throw during the first load. The dataTableModel scenario only uses "Flows", so no test catches it. `emptyTitle` (120) and `emptyDescription` (300) fit the kit's limits; only `loadingLabel` does not. Either cap the caption at 72 or define the label differently.

The focus rules contradict the design's promise that "keyboard focus is never lost" (Decision 4) and the DATA_KEYBOARD text "Activates the button; focus then moves to the table or to Try again." Under task 2.2, `retry` is `hidden` outside `error`. Activating "Try again" or "Start over" moves the state from `error` to `loading`, which unmounts the focused button, and `focusAfterChange(error→loading)` is `none`. A first-page `loading`→`loaded` (no items before) is also `none`, so focus stays lost. Load more is also "`aria-disabled=\"true\"` and inert while `busy`". If inert means the HTML `inert` attribute, the browser drops focus from Load more every time it is pressed. No scenario covers the `none` branch or any transition out of `error`. The author must state where focus goes after retry or restart, and what "inert" means.

Behaviour that lives only in the `.tsx` files has no test that can decide it, and those files are merged with only `pnpm run typecheck` (design § Test plan). The Failure cases table promises "Double submit … ignored while busy", and the requirement is titled "Submitting sends valid values once". The guard exists only in Form.tsx ("ignores the event while busy") and SchemaForm.tsx ("ignored while busy"). `submitValues` has no guard and its scenario calls it once. Other untested wiring: DataTable's effect that calls `list.load()` when idle, the retry and Load more handlers, moving focus after `focusAfterChange`, Form focusing the first invalid control once per attempt, and SchemaForm resetting its state when `schema` changes. Either move the busy guard into a tested `.ts` function or give it a scenario a test can decide.

Task 4.1 conflicts with itself on enum properties without a `type`. The kind list allows the enum kind with "`type` absent or `\"string\"`", but the fault order checks "`type` missing … (`the property has no type`)" before the kind's keywords. Read literally, `{ enum: ["a","b"] }` becomes unsupported. No scenario covers an enum without `type`.

Some visible `Unsupported:` reasons and labels are not fixed, so tests cannot pin them: a pattern that is not text or is longer than 200 characters (only `pattern is not a valid expression` is given), an array with no `items`, a `required` list with a name that fails `isFieldName`, and the label to use when `title` itself is invalid (`title must be text of 1 to 80 characters`). It is also not stated whether `validateValues` compiles patterns with the `u` flag that task 4.1 uses to accept them.

The data kit takes the classes `.ui-button` and `.ui-visually-hidden` from add-web-ui-kit's theme.css (design § Context). The visible add-web-ui-kit spec ("The theme uses only tokens") lists only `.ui-empty`, `.ui-loading`, `.ui-error`, `.ui-dialog`, `.ui-toasts` and `.ui-toast`, and no data-kit test checks for the two. DataTable's always-present `aria-live` announcement region depends on `.ui-visually-hidden` to stay invisible.

`fieldModel` requires `idPrefix` to match `^[A-Za-z0-9:_-]{1,64}$`, and SchemaForm gets its prefix from React's `useId()`. Whether those ids match depends on the React version, which the material does not state; `useId`'s format has changed across 19.x releases. If they don't match, every SchemaForm render throws, and no test would notice.

"Decisions made while writing 1" says that if add-web-ui-kit's scenario "Documentation matches the component files" recurses into subdirectories, "the orchestrator must change it". An unattended run has no orchestrator to ask. The risk is small because the data-kit `.tsx` stubs are already on the base branch when add-web-ui-kit is delivered, but the open contingency should be settled in the spec.

DataTable's effect calls `list.load()` whenever the state is `idle`, and `reset()` returns the list to `idle`. Security §2 says "a page that ends a session calls `reset()`". If the table is still mounted, it then fetches again at once with no session. The spec does not say whether that is intended. SchemaForm's behaviour after a `submitted` result (keep or clear values, clear errors) is also unstated.

findings.text: Task 4.2 tells the implementer to run a bare `INSERT INTO ursitoare.tenant (tenant_id, name, review_profile) VALUES ($1, $2, 'solo') ON CONFLICT (tenant_id) DO NOTHING` through a plain `createPool(ownerUrl, { max: 1 })`, with no tenant setting. Other parts of the plan say this insert will be refused. `ursitoare.tenant` is under RLS: add-api-pep design says "table `ursitoare.tenant` … under RLS", the identity requirement says "A tenant profile is read under row-level security", and this unit's own scenario reads the table "as tenant B". add-identity-model design decision 2 also says forced security binds the owner: "a raw owner statement sees and writes nothing". design.md § Context states two facts next to each other and does not reconcile them: "a reset re-runs every seed" (`10-database`, `20-web`, `25-oidc`, `27-tenant-b`) and "`ensureDefaultTenant` refuses a second tenant". Every journey test takes `fresh_state`, which POSTs `/reset`. So from the second test on, and in the M0 and web-kit journeys that must keep passing, the already-delivered database and oidc parts re-seed while tenant B exists. The scenario "Tenant B is created and its organisation provisioned" covers `oidcPart.seed` running again after `tenantBPart.seed`. Nothing covers the database part's seed in that state, and no Node test runs a full reset with tenant B present: `stack.seed.test.ts` starts the stack once and never resets. The spec does not say what a reset does to `ursitoare.tenant`, or how the default-tenant seed behaves once a second tenant exists. If that seed fails, the fix lies outside this unit's file list.

The requirement "The CSRF header is added only to same-origin state-changing requests" says the header goes on "every non-GET request to a root-relative URL", and the proposal says "every non-GET request". The scenario and task 2.1 make `isStateChanging` false for `HEAD` and `OPTIONS` as well. The requirement text and the proposal should say "state-changing (not GET, HEAD or OPTIONS)".

Several stated behaviours have no scenario, either in the Node tests or in the journey: the sign-out button ignoring clicks with `aria-disabled="true"` while a sign-out runs (decision 9); the error toast with `messageFor(code)` and the button becoming usable again after a failed sign-out (decision 6 and the Failure cases table); `SignInPage` setting `document.title` to `Sign in · Ursitoare` and restoring it; and `useSession` aborting on unmount and ignoring `AbortError`.

Task 4.4 has the `users` fixture raise `RuntimeError` "when `e2e_profile` is not `fake`". The only Python names listed as taken are `fresh_state` and `DEFAULT_CONTROL_URL`. `e2e_profile` (fixture, function or variable) is not declared anywhere in the material.

In the scenario "The control listener serves seed data to the test process only", the ending "and 405 with `allow: POST`, 404 for the last two" can be read two ways for `GET /reset` and `POST /nowhere`. The e2e engine has a database and a policy engine, so `GET /api/v1/me` without a cookie answers 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`, not the 503 that add-api-pep gives when `PepDeps.pool` is null.

As design.md Context states, add-web-shell's `navItems()` / `registry.nav()` called with no argument hides entries that have a `capability`. `createFeatureRegistry().nav` also works when passed unbound, as `visibleNav(state, registry.nav)` does.
The Node test runner gives each test file its own process, so `registerMessages` calls in `messages.test.ts` do not reach other test files.
`from conftest import assert_accessible` works under the e2e suite's current pytest import mode (the default, prepend).
add-web-shell's client produces the codes `NETWORK_ERROR`, `HTTP_ERROR` and `INVALID_RESPONSE` that the catalogue calls client codes.
As design decision 10 states, injecting axe with `page.evaluate(source)` keeps the page's CSP and produces no CSP console message.

batch_acceptance does not apply to a unit, minor: The proposal says the shell 'lists only the entries whose `capability` the answer holds'. In the browser, no M0 feature has a `capability`, so `test_me_success_keeps_the_nav` (capabilities `["read_flow"]`) only shows that 'Home' is still there. Hiding and showing entries is proved only by the Node `visibleNav` scenario. That is acceptable, but the browser journey does not show this outcome.

findings.text: design.md Rules says `findInlineStyleUse` reports lines holding `style=`, `<style` or `setAttribute("style"` (double quotes). But sample line 3 in the scenario 'The web sources have no inline styles' is `el.setAttribute('style', 'a')` (single quotes), and the scenario says it must be reported. Read literally, the rule misses that line. The scenario decides, but the rule text should say both quote forms.

Scenario 'The M0 pages pass' requires that 'no console message mentions "Content Security Policy"'. Task 9.1 only tells the four `e2e/test_m0_skeleton.py` tests to call `assert_accessible(page)` after their last step. No task adds a console listener to those tests or says one already exists, so nothing is assigned to check this THEN clause.

The proposal says 'the built app loads `tokens.css` and `theme.css` from `/assets/`'. The CSS files are imported from `web/src/main.tsx`, so the build will likely bundle them into one hashed stylesheet rather than serve two named files. No scenario checks this claim, so the outcome as written is neither accurate nor checkable. It should name what is actually observable, e.g. the `.ui-*` rules being applied with no CSP message.

`test_assert_accessible_accepts_a_named_button` uses `page.set_content(...)` but the spec never gives the content. A bare `<button>Save</button>` document has no `<html lang>` and no `<title>`, so axe would report `html-has-lang` and `document-title` (both serious, wcag2a) and this 'accepts' test would fail. The scenario should give the full document: lang, title and a labelled button.

Task 9.1 / design 'Decisions made while writing': a serious or critical axe finding in the M0 shell may only be fixed in `web/src/app/shell.css`, 'nowhere else outside the kit'. Some serious or critical WCAG-A rules are about markup, not CSS (`link-name`, `list`/`listitem`, `html-has-lang`, `document-title`, `button-name`). If the M0 pages fail on one of these, the implementer cannot meet both the scope rule and the acceptance scenario. The spec should say what to do in that case, e.g. allow `Shell.tsx` or `web/index.html`, or stop the unit.

Design decision 5 and task 7.1 define `load`, sharing, caching and abort for `CapabilityLoader`. They do not say what happens when `reset()` runs while a `/me` request is still in flight: is the late `ready` answer cached, or dropped? This matters because the hand-off says `add-web-sign-in` calls `reset()` on sign-out, and a stale `ready` (with its `csrfToken`) could outlive the session.

Several toast-queue rules are left open (design decision 9 and the 'Duplicates, limits and invalid specs' scenario):
- The scenario says a duplicate push gives 'a refreshed expiry', but gives no clock movement and no expected `expiresAt`.
- It does not say whether the deduplicated item moves to the newest position, which decides what `maxVisible` drops next.
